# Requirements Analysis Questions

Initial description: Create a 3D version of the game

## Q1. Source game

Which existing game should this 3D version reproduce?

- A. The game already exists in another repository or folder; I will provide its location
- B. The game exists as a published title or website; I will name or link it
- C. The game is described in rules or design documents; I will provide them
- D. There is no existing game; define a new game from my description
- E. Use the current project, despite no game code being present
- X. Other (please specify)

[Answer]:

## Q2. Fidelity

How closely should the 3D version follow the source game?

- A. Faithful conversion: preserve rules, content, progression, and overall feel
- B. Preserve the core mechanics but redesign presentation and supporting systems
- C. Create a small playable 3D adaptation of the central gameplay loop
- D. Use the source only as inspiration for a substantially new game
- X. Other (please specify)

[Answer]:

## Q3. Target platform and controls

What is the primary target?

- A. Desktop web browser with keyboard and mouse
- B. Desktop application with keyboard and mouse
- C. Mobile web or app with touch controls
- D. Game console with controller input
- E. Desktop and mobile web with responsive controls
- X. Other (please specify)

[Answer]:

## Q4. Camera and presentation

What 3D viewpoint should the game use?

- A. First-person
- B. Third-person follow camera
- C. Fixed or cinematic camera
- D. Isometric or top-down 3D
- E. Choose the viewpoint that best preserves the source gameplay
- X. Other (please specify)

[Answer]:

## Q5. Visual direction

What visual target should guide the first version?

- A. Simple low-poly visuals using generated geometric assets
- B. Stylized visuals with custom models, materials, lighting, and effects
- C. Realistic visuals
- D. Match the source game's established visual identity
- E. Prioritize gameplay using placeholders that can be replaced later
- X. Other (please specify)

[Answer]:

## Q6. First release boundary

What must the first approved version include?

- A. One polished playable level or scenario demonstrating the full core loop
- B. All source-game gameplay and content converted to 3D
- C. A playable prototype focused on movement, camera, and the defining mechanic
- D. A reusable 3D foundation plus a representative subset of content
- X. Other (please specify)

[Answer]:

## Q7. Technical constraints

How should the technology be selected?

- A. Use a browser-native 3D stack and choose the specific framework
- B. Use Unity
- C. Use Godot
- D. Use Unreal Engine
- E. Choose the simplest stack that satisfies the selected platform and scope
- X. Other (please specify)

[Answer]:

## Q8. Quality target

Which baseline should the first release meet?

- A. Stable 60 FPS on a typical modern desktop, keyboard accessibility, saved progress, and automated tests for core rules
- B. Stable 30 FPS on the selected platform and automated tests for core rules
- C. Prototype quality: playable core loop without persistence or formal accessibility targets
- D. Define measurable quality targets after reviewing the source game
- X. Other (please specify)

[Answer]:
